flashcards.q: What is the canonical chain of product thinking, and in which direction do you argue vs build?
flashcards.a: Problem -> outcome -> solution. Argue UP the chain from any proposed solution to its implied outcome and problem; build DOWN the chain once problem and outcome are fixed. Solution debates held before the outcome is set are unfalsifiable politics.

flashcards.q: Name the five components of a defensible problem statement.
flashcards.a: Who (segment, sized), what pain (observable behavior, not adjectives), when/how often, what it costs them and the business, and why now — a forcing function with a date (capability threshold crossed, regulation effective date, competitor move).

flashcards.q: What three properties distinguish a real outcome from an output in disguise?
flashcards.a: It measures user behavior (not delivery telemetry), it has a trusted baseline/counterfactual, and it carries guardrails with pre-agreed thresholds. 'Ship AI copilot by Q3' is an output; 'cut median time-to-first-insight from 9 min to 3 without p95 regressions' is an outcome.

flashcards.q: Why generate at least three solution candidates before evaluating any?
flashcards.a: Because single-candidate evaluation collapses into advocacy — you defend instead of compare. The discipline matters more than idea quality; it also exposes the hammer-looking-for-nails failure where the problem statement is written after the solution choice.

flashcards.q: Translate a +25% recsys engagement lift into dollars — sketch the chain.
flashcards.a: +25% engaged interactions -> ~+20% session length (measured) -> +5pts 7-day return rate (cohort data) -> revenue via an LTV model ($0.31 ARPU per D7 pt) x 4.2M MAU ~= $6.5M/mo face value, presented as a $4-8M/yr band because the ARPU link is modeled, not measured.

flashcards.q: Why present a dollar band rather than a point estimate?
flashcards.a: Finance re-derives your numbers; a range with named assumptions survives scrutiny while false precision invites distrust of everything else. The band also carries decision info: if even the pessimistic end clears project cost, that's the actual question answered.

flashcards.q: Compute the COGS floor of an AI feature doing 10M req/mo at 2K tokens/request with $3/Mtok pricing.
flashcards.a: 10M x 2000 / 1e6 = 20M tokens/mo... precisely 10e6*2e3=20B tokens/mo /1e6 = 20,000 Mtok x $3 = $60K/mo = $720K/yr COGS. The feature must move >$720K/yr of value or the margin is negative.

flashcards.q: What is the kill question and why must it be written before building?
flashcards.a: The cheaply observable result that would make you cancel. Written before kickoff it acts as pre-registration: skipping it is how zombie projects survive, because after launch every stakeholder reinterprets ambiguous results in favor of continuing.

flashcards.q: Which work types should NOT be forced into outcome/growth framing?
flashcards.a: Constraint work (security, compliance, SRE error budgets) argues in risk terms (expected loss avoided); exploratory spikes argue bounded-cost/binary-answer; platform migrations argue avoided-future-cost. Mislabeled frames produce fake numbers finance ignores.

flashcards.q: What makes a guardrail veto non-political?
flashcards.a: The threshold was written down and agreed BEFORE results existed. A veto based on pre-registered thresholds is enforcement; a veto based on taste after seeing results is politics, regardless of who is right.

flashcards.q: Roughly how much is two engineers for two quarters in opportunity cost?
flashcards.a: Fully loaded cost commonly lands around $400-600K. Any proposal whose best-case value doesn't clear that floor dies on arithmetic alone — present the ledger and let the room draw the conclusion.

flashcards.q: What is the common structural feature of Amazon PR/FAQ, Netflix memos, Stripe RFCs, Google design docs?
flashcards.a: The value claim and the cost claim live adjacent in the SAME document, so neither can be argued in isolation. Teams splitting them across documents (PM deck vs eng spreadsheet) systematically underprice projects.
